Intake record showing the consumer's age
ChildLine request form copy and verification in each employee, rostered individual, office staff and owner file
Quarterly file audit checklist
Records of adverse decisions

policies.title: Provisional Hiring: Eligibility Conditions
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, hiring/records manager, and all direct care worker and office staff applicants considered for provisional hire at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define when [AGENCY NAME] may hire or roster an individual provisionally while criminal history reports or ChildLine verification are still pending, and to make sure no provisional hire reaches a consumer before the required competency is shown.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires or rosters an individual provisionally only if every condition in this policy is met. This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.54(a)(1), (a)(2), (a)(3) and (a)(4). (a)(1) Applied and forms supplied: The applicant has applied for a criminal history report and ChildLine verification, as applicable, and has given the agency a copy of the completed request forms. (a)(2) No disqualifying knowledge: The agency has no knowledge that would disqualify the applicant under 18 Pa.C.S. §4911. (a)(3) Sworn statement: The applicant swears or affirms in writing that the applicant is not disqualified under Chapter 611, using the Provisional Hire Sworn Statement. (a)(4) Competency first: The agency does not assign or refer a provisional hire to any consumer until the competency requirements of §611.55 are met (see CMP-01). Monitoring, time limits and termination are covered in PRV-02. Provisional hire is a permission, not a right. The Administrator may decline it for any applicant.

definitions.definition: An individual hired or rostered for work before the criminal history report or ChildLine verification (as applicable) has been received.
The completed applications the applicant submitted to request the criminal history report and ChildLine verification.
The applicant's signed written statement, sworn or affirmed, that the applicant is not disqualified under Chapter 611.
Any information known to the agency, from any source, that would disqualify the applicant under 18 Pa.C.S. §4911 or under the prohibitions covered in CBC-02 and CAC-01.

procedures: The hiring/records manager first completes the interview and reference steps in HIR-01 for the applicant. The applicant is not considered for provisional hire until those steps are finished.

The hiring/records manager tells the applicant that provisional hire is possible only if every condition in this policy is met, and gives the applicant the request instructions and forms for the criminal history report and, if CAC-01 applies, the ChildLine verification.

The applicant submits the requests. The applicant gives the agency a copy of each completed request form on or before the date provisional hire is considered. The hiring/records manager checks that each form is complete and dated and files it in the applicant's file.
If a required request form is missing or incomplete, no provisional hire is made. The Administrator documents the reason in the file.

The Administrator reviews the application, interview notes, references and any other information to confirm the agency has no knowledge that would disqualify the applicant under 18 Pa.C.S. §4911. The Administrator documents the review and signs the Provisional Hire Checklist.
If the Administrator learns of disqualifying information at any time, provisional hire is refused or ended at once, and the process in CBC-02 and CBC-04 is followed.

The applicant signs the Provisional Hire Sworn Statement, swearing or affirming in writing that the applicant is not disqualified under Chapter 611. The Administrator or hiring/records manager witnesses it and dates it.
The Administrator completes the Provisional Hire Checklist showing that (a)(1), (a)(2) and (a)(3) are met, and records the provisional hire start date, which PRV-02 uses to calculate the end date.

The hiring/records manager confirms that the applicant meets the competency requirements in CMP-01 before any consumer assignment or referral. The scheduler is told in writing that the person is on provisional status.

The scheduler does not assign or refer the provisional hire to any consumer, and the Administrator does not authorize any consumer contact, until the competency route is documented in the worker's file under CMP-01 and CMP-04.
Once competency is documented, the Administrator releases the provisional hire for assignment in writing. PRV-02 monitoring, supervision and time limits begin to apply to all assignments.

The hiring/records manager keeps the request forms, Sworn Statement and Provisional Hire Checklist in the worker's file under HIR-02 and PER-03. The Administrator reviews the log of provisional hires monthly.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether provisional hire is allowed; confirms no disqualifying knowledge; signs the checklist; releases the worker for assignment after competency.
Collects request forms and the Sworn Statement; completes the file; confirms competency documentation.
Does not assign or refer any provisional hire without written release by the Administrator.
Applies for the reports, gives copies of the request forms, and signs the Sworn Statement truthfully.

documentation: Copies of completed criminal history and ChildLine request forms
Provisional Hire Sworn Statement
Provisional Hire Checklist signed by the Administrator, with start date
Written competency documentation and release for assignment
Provisional hire log

policies.title: Provisional Hire Monitoring, Time Limits and Termination
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, supervisors, scheduler, hiring/records manager and all provisionally hired direct care workers and office staff at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure that provisional hires are monitored while reports are pending, that provisional hires serving consumers under 18 are supervised, that the maximum provisional period is never exceeded, and that anyone who is disqualified or misses the deadline is removed immediately.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.54(a)(5), (a)(6), (a)(7) and (b). (a)(5) Monitoring: [AGENCY NAME] monitors each provisional hire awaiting a criminal background check through random direct observation and consumer feedback, and documents the results in the individual's file. (a)(6) Minors: A provisional hire awaiting child abuse clearance who will serve a consumer under 18 is directly supervised, or accompanied by another direct care worker. (a)(7) Time limits: Provisional hire may not exceed 30 days for an individual who has been a Pennsylvania resident for two or more years, or 90 days for one who has not. (b) Termination: If the reports show disqualification, or the individual does not provide the ChildLine verification or criminal history report within the provisional period, the agency terminates the individual or removes the individual from the roster immediately.

definitions.definition: The time from the provisional hire start date recorded on the Provisional Hire Checklist (PRV-01) until the required report or verification is received, up to the maximum allowed.
An unannounced or unscheduled visit by a supervisor or designee to watch the worker's performance in the consumer's home.
Direct input from the consumer or representative on the provisional hire's performance, gathered by phone or in person.
A supervisor or another direct care worker is physically present with the provisional hire throughout the shift with a consumer under 18.
An individual who has resided in Pennsylvania for two or more years, as documented in CBC-01.

procedures: On the provisional hire start date, the hiring/records manager enters the individual in the Provisional Hire Tracker with the start date, the reports pending, the Pennsylvania residency determination, and the end date.

The hiring/records manager determines the maximum period using the residency documentation under CBC-01: 30 days if the individual has been a Pennsylvania resident for 2 or more years, and 90 days otherwise. The end date is the start date plus that number of days, and is shown on the tracker.
If residency cannot be documented, the 90-day limit applies. The hiring/records manager does not use the 30-day limit unless the documentation supports it.
The hiring/records manager reviews the tracker every week, and sends a reminder to the Administrator and the individual at 10 days and again at 5 days before the end date.

For an individual awaiting a criminal background check, the Clinical/Operations Supervisor makes at least one random direct observation of the worker with a consumer within the first 14 days of assignment and at further intervals chosen by the Administrator, before the provisional period ends.
The supervisor also contacts the consumer or representative to ask for feedback, using the Provisional Hire Feedback Form, within 7 days of the first assignment and at each observation.
The supervisor documents each observation and each feedback contact on the form, with date, time, findings and any corrective action, and files it in the worker's file the same day.

Any concern about consumer safety, abuse, neglect or exploitation seen in observation or reported in feedback is reported to the Administrator at once and handled under SAF-01 and SAF-02. The Administrator may remove the worker from assignment pending the reports.

Before assigning a provisional hire awaiting child abuse clearance to a consumer under 18, the scheduler checks the intake record and the tracker. The scheduler schedules a supervisor or another direct care worker to be present throughout each shift.
The supervisor or accompanying worker signs the shift supervision log for each visit with the minor. The log is kept in the provisional hire's file.

When a report or verification is received, the hiring/records manager gives it to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator decides under CBC-02 and CAC-01. On clearance, the individual is marked as no longer provisional on the tracker and the file is completed.

If a report or verification shows disqualification, the Administrator terminates the individual or removes the individual from the roster immediately, on the same day the report is reviewed. The scheduler removes the worker from every assignment and arranges replacement coverage under SVC-06.

If the end date arrives and a required criminal history report or ChildLine verification has not been provided, the Administrator terminates the individual or removes the individual from the roster immediately, at the close of business on the end date. No extension is granted.
The Administrator documents each termination or removal, the reason and the date in the file. Appeal information is given under CBC-04 if a decision rests on criminal records.
The Administrator reviews the tracker monthly and reports the number of provisional hires, any overdue items and any terminations at the quality review meeting under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Makes disqualification and termination decisions the same day; approves removal from assignment; reviews the tracker monthly.
Maintains the tracker; calculates end dates; sends reminders; files reports and verification.
Performs random direct observations; collects consumer feedback; supervises provisional hires serving minors.
Enforces supervision or accompaniment for minors; removes terminated workers from the schedule.
Follows up on report requests, supplies reports promptly, and complies with supervision.

documentation: Provisional Hire Tracker with start date, residency determination and end date
Residency documentation
Random observation records and Provisional Hire Feedback Forms
Shift supervision logs for provisional hires serving consumers under 18
Termination or removal records
Monthly tracker review notes

policies.title: Establishing Competency Before Assignment or Referral
policies.applies_to: All direct care workers employed by, or referred through, [AGENCY NAME], including provisional hires, and all staff who hire, schedule, assign or refer workers
policies.purpose: To make sure that no direct care worker is assigned to a consumer, or referred to a consumer, until the worker has shown competency through one of the routes allowed by 28 Pa. Code §611.55(a), and to make sure the route used is recorded in the worker's file.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.55(a)(1)–(3). [AGENCY NAME] will not assign or refer a direct care worker to any consumer unless, before the first assignment or referral, the worker has met at least one of the following routes: (1) the worker holds a valid Pennsylvania nurse's license; (2) the worker has passed the agency's competency examination; or (3) the worker has completed an approved training program. Approved training programs are: (i) a training program offered by [AGENCY NAME] or by another entity that meets the content and testing standards described in CMP-02 and CMP-03; (ii) a home health aide training program that meets the federal home health aide training standard named in §611.55(a)(3)(ii); (iii) the Pennsylvania Department of Education nurse aide certification and training program; (iv) a training program that meets the standards of a Medicaid Waiver or other publicly funded home and community-based services (HCBS) program in which [AGENCY NAME] participates, such as the OBRA Waiver or Community HealthChoices; or (v) another program that the Department of Health identifies. The reference to the federal home health aide training standard is accepted by [AGENCY NAME] as a training standard only. It does not make [AGENCY NAME] a Medicare-certified home health agency and does not change its licensure under Chapter 611. The route used for each worker will be recorded in the worker's file. A worker who has not satisfied a route will not be placed on the schedule, assigned or referred, even for a single shift, regardless of staffing needs.

definitions.definition: An individual who provides direct, hands-on, non-medical home care services to a consumer on behalf of [AGENCY NAME], whether as an employee or through a referral arrangement.
Demonstrated knowledge and skill needed to perform the assigned home care tasks safely, established by one of the routes listed in this policy.
One of the three options under §611.55(a): (1) a valid Pennsylvania nurse's license, (2) a passed agency competency examination, or (3) completion of an approved training program.
A program listed in the Policy section of this document under item (3)(i) through (3)(v), including a Medicaid Waiver or other publicly funded HCBS training program.
Placing a worker with a consumer to provide services, or giving a consumer the worker's name for the purpose of providing services.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is responsible for this policy. No worker may be scheduled for, assigned to or referred to a consumer until the Hiring Coordinator has documented a route to competency in the worker's file.

At the time of application, the Hiring Coordinator asks every applicant to state whether they hold a Pennsylvania nurse's license, a certificate from an approved training program, or neither. The Coordinator records the answer on the Competency Route Verification Form.

Route 1, nurse license: the Hiring Coordinator verifies on the Commonwealth's online professional license verification system that the license is valid and in good standing. The Coordinator prints or saves the verification page showing the license type, number, status and date checked, and places it in the worker's file.

Route 2, agency competency exam: the Clinical Reviewer or other qualified exam administrator designated by the Administrator gives the agency's competency examination, as described in CMP-02 and CMP-03, and scores it the same day. The signed and dated exam and score sheet go in the worker's file. A worker who does not pass is not assigned and may retake the exam only after remedial instruction, which is documented.

Route 3, approved training program: the Hiring Coordinator obtains a copy of the worker's certificate, transcript or completion letter. It must show the worker's name, the program name and sponsor, the completion date, and the hours or content completed.

For a training program run by [AGENCY NAME] or another entity (item 3(i)), the Hiring Coordinator confirms that the program covers the content and testing standards in CMP-02 and, for workers who will provide personal care, CMP-03. The Coordinator keeps a copy of the program outline with the file or in the program binder.

For a home health aide program (item 3(ii)), the Hiring Coordinator confirms from the certificate or program outline that the program was a home health aide training program meeting the federal standard named in §611.55(a)(3)(ii). The Coordinator notes in the file that this is accepted as a training standard only and does not alter the agency's licensure status.

For a Pennsylvania Department of Education nurse aide program (item 3(iii)), the Hiring Coordinator obtains the nurse aide training or certification documentation and records the program name and completion date.

For a Medicaid Waiver or other publicly funded HCBS training program (item 3(iv)), the Hiring Coordinator confirms that [AGENCY NAME] participates in that program, such as the OBRA Waiver or Community HealthChoices. The Coordinator also obtains proof of the worker's completion and keeps a copy of the program standards or the payer's training requirement relied on.

For any other program the Department of Health identifies (item 3(v)), the Hiring Coordinator obtains a written copy of the Department's identification of that program, such as a notice, letter or published list, and attaches it with the worker's proof of completion.

If the worker's documentation is unclear, expired, incomplete or cannot be verified, the Hiring Coordinator does not accept it. The worker must then take the agency's competency exam (Route 2) or complete an approved program before assignment.

Before placing the worker on the schedule or giving a consumer the worker's name, the Scheduler checks the worker's file for a completed Competency Route Verification Form signed by the Hiring Coordinator. If the form is missing, the Scheduler stops and notifies the Administrator.

The Hiring Coordinator records on the form the route used (1, 2, or 3 with the sub-item), the evidence reviewed, the date of verification and the Coordinator's signature. The Administrator countersigns the form when the file is complete.

When a worker's file is reviewed under HIR-02, PER-03 and CMP-04, the reviewer confirms that the competency route is still documented and that the evidence supports it. Any gap is reported to the Administrator the same day, and the worker is removed from assignments until the gap is corrected.

If a worker relies on a nurse's license (Route 1) and the license later lapses, is suspended or is revoked, the Administrator removes the worker from assignments immediately. The worker may return only after another route is satisfied or the license is reinstated and re-verified.

Once a year, the Administrator or designee audits a sample of worker files, and all files when a deficiency is found, to confirm that every active worker has a documented route that was satisfied before the first assignment. Results are reported in the quality assurance review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Owns this policy, countersigns Competency Route Verification Forms, removes any worker without a documented route, and reviews the annual file audit.
Collects and verifies evidence for the route used, completes the Competency Route Verification Form, and places all evidence in the worker's file before assignment.

responsibilities.role: Clinical Reviewer or designated exam administrator
responsibilities.duty: Gives and scores the agency competency exam and documents remedial instruction and retakes.
Confirms a signed competency verification is in the file before scheduling, assigning or referring any worker.
Provides accurate and complete training or licensure documentation and does not begin work with a consumer until told in writing that competency is established.

Printout of the license verification for workers using the nurse license route

Training program certificate, transcript or completion letter and program outline for workers using the approved program route

Annual file audit results and corrective actions

policies.title: Competency Exam and Training Content: Core Topics for All Direct Care Workers
policies.applies_to: All direct care workers, employed or rostered, before any assignment or referral to a consumer; the Administrator, the supervising nurse or experienced administrator who reviews the exam, and the staff who administer it.
policies.purpose: To make sure every direct care worker has the knowledge needed to work safely and respectfully in a consumer's home, and to show a surveyor that the agency's competency exam or training addresses each core topic required by 28 Pa. Code §611.55(b).
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not assign a direct care worker to any consumer until the worker has passed a competency exam or completed competency training that covers, at a minimum, every topic in 28 Pa. Code §611.55(b). This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.55(b)(1) through (b)(10): (b)(1) Confidentiality; (b)(2) Consumer control and the independent living philosophy; (b)(3) Instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs); (b)(4) Recognizing changes in the consumer that need to be addressed; (b)(5) Basic infection control; (b)(6) Universal precautions; (b)(7) Handling of emergencies; (b)(8) Documentation; (b)(9) Recognizing and reporting abuse or neglect; and (b)(10) Dealing with difficult behaviors. Workers who will provide personal care must also meet CMP-03. The agency may use an exam, training, or both, and the content must stay current. A nurse or an experienced administrator reviews the exam before it is first used and whenever it is changed. The agency keeps the exam, the answer key and each worker's results. Confidentiality content is aligned with the agency's HIPAA privacy practices (45 CFR 164.530), and infection control and universal precautions content is aligned with the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard (29 CFR 1910.1030).

definitions.definition: The individual who receives home care services from the agency, as the term is defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5. This manual also uses the terms client and participant.

The consumer's right to direct how, when and by whom services are delivered, as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5. It is the basis of the independent living philosophy: the consumer makes the decisions, and the worker supports them.
An individual employed by or rostered with the agency who provides direct consumer contact and services, as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5.

The household and community tasks that support independent living, such as meal preparation, shopping, laundry and light housekeeping. The definition is taken from section 802a of the Health Care Facilities Act (35 P.S. §448.802a), through 28 Pa. Code §611.5. The agency's IADL reference sheet is built from that definition.

Infection control practices that treat all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious, including hand hygiene, gloves and other personal protective equipment, and safe disposal of contaminated materials.
A registered nurse (RN) or licensed practical nurse (LPN), as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a written Core Competency Exam and a matching training curriculum. Each lists the ten required topics, and each question or training module is labeled with the §611.55(b) item it addresses.

Confidentiality (b)(1): The exam covers what is private about a consumer (health, finances, address, schedule, photos, social media and conversations), when information may be shared, how to protect records and devices, and who the worker reports a privacy problem to.

Consumer control and independent living (b)(2): The exam covers the consumer's right to make choices, including choices the worker would not make, how to offer options instead of taking over, and how to raise safety concerns without overriding the consumer's decisions.
IADLs (b)(3): The exam covers the IADL list drawn from 35 P.S. §448.802a, how to perform each task, and which tasks are outside the non-medical scope of the agency (see SVC-01).

Changes in the consumer (b)(4): The exam covers how to recognize changes in the consumer that need attention, such as new confusion, falls, skin changes, appetite or mood changes, and pain. It also covers whom to tell and by when, and when to call 911 (see SVC-08).

Infection control and universal precautions (b)(5)-(b)(6): The exam and training cover hand hygiene, gloves and other personal protective equipment, cleaning and disinfecting, handling soiled linens, safe handling of sharps and body fluids, illness reporting and exposure reporting (see SAF-03). Training includes a hands-on hand-washing and glove-removal demonstration.

Emergencies (b)(7): The exam covers medical emergencies, falls, fire, severe weather, power loss, and a consumer who cannot be reached. It covers when to call 911, how to stay with the consumer, who at the agency to notify, and how to complete an incident report (see SVC-08, SAF-02 and SAF-04).

Documentation (b)(8): The exam covers accurate, timely and factual notes and timesheets, including how to record what was done and observed, how to correct an error without erasing it, and electronic visit verification (see SVC-07).

Abuse and neglect (b)(9): The exam covers the types and signs of abuse, neglect, exploitation and abandonment. It covers the worker's duty to report immediately to the supervisor and the reporting steps in SAF-01, and it states that retaliation for reporting is prohibited.

Difficult behaviors (b)(10): The exam covers how to respond to confusion, agitation, aggression, refusal of care, and verbal or sexual harassment. It covers de-escalation, setting boundaries, leaving an unsafe situation, and reporting to the supervisor (see SAF-05).

The exam uses written, oral or demonstration formats so that workers with limited reading skills or limited English can be fairly evaluated, and interpretation or translation is provided on request. The passing score is 80 percent. Every question on abuse and neglect reporting, emergencies and universal precautions must be answered correctly. Missed questions are reviewed with the worker and re-tested before the worker is cleared.

Before first use, and again after any content change, a nurse or experienced administrator reviews the exam and answer key and signs and dates the review. The Administrator keeps the reviewer's name and credential on file.

The designated trainer or supervisor administers the exam or training. The trainer records the worker's name, date, method, score and the person who scored it. A worker who does not pass receives remedial training and may re-test. The worker is not assigned to consumers until a passing result is recorded.

The Administrator files the completed exam, answer key and results according to CMP-04 and PER-03. A summary of the topics covered is added to the worker's competency record so that each §611.55(b) item can be verified by a surveyor.
The Administrator reviews the exam and curriculum at least annually, when regulations change, and after any incident that shows a training gap. Revisions follow GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the exam and training content, ensures all ten topics are covered, and does not clear or assign a worker who has not passed.
Reviews the exam and answer key for accuracy and completeness and signs and dates the review.
Administers and scores the exam or training, documents results, and arranges remedial training.
Completes the exam or training and applies the content in the consumer's home.

policies.title: Competency Content for Workers Providing Personal Care
policies.applies_to: Direct care workers who will provide personal care, and the nurses or qualified supervisors who evaluate them, plus schedulers who assign workers.
policies.purpose: To make sure that any worker who provides hands-on personal care has been tested and trained on each required personal care topic, in addition to the core topics, before being assigned to do so.
policies.policy: In addition to the core content in CMP-02, [AGENCY NAME] requires every direct care worker who will provide personal care to complete an exam or training that addresses each topic in 28 Pa. Code §611.55(c). This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.55(c)(1) Bathing, shaving, grooming and dressing; (c)(2) Hair, skin and mouth care; (c)(3) Assistance with ambulation and transferring; (c)(4) Meal preparation and feeding; (c)(5) Toileting; and (c)(6) Assistance with self-administered medications. Skills are shown by return demonstration observed by a nurse or qualified supervisor, and the results are recorded on the agency's Personal Care Skills Checklist. A worker who has been cleared only for companionship or IADL tasks is never assigned personal care tasks. Medication tasks are limited to assistance with self-administration (see SVC-05).

definitions.definition: Hands-on, non-medical help with activities such as bathing, grooming, dressing, mouth care, mobility and transferring, feeding, toileting and assistance with self-administered medication.
Socialization, support and IADL help as described in 28 Pa. Code §611.5. They do not include hands-on personal care.
The worker performs the task while an evaluator watches and checks each step, rather than only describing it.
A supervisor designated in writing by the Administrator who has been trained in the personal care skills and is competent to evaluate them. A nurse may always serve as evaluator.
Medication that the consumer takes personally, with a worker providing only limited support such as reminders, opening a container, or handing the consumer the medication, as limited in SVC-05.

procedures: At hire, the Administrator determines whether the worker will provide personal care. The determination is recorded in the worker's file as 'Companionship/IADL only' or 'Personal care cleared'.
A worker designated for personal care completes the core exam (CMP-02) and the personal care exam or training covering all six topics in §611.55(c).

Training on bathing, shaving, grooming and dressing (c)(1) covers privacy and dignity, water temperature checks, skin protection, fall prevention in the bathroom and dressing techniques for limited mobility.
Training on hair, skin and mouth care (c)(2) covers hair washing and brushing, skin inspection, moisturizing, noticing and reporting skin breakdown or redness, and denture and mouth care.

Training on ambulation and transferring (c)(3) covers body mechanics, use of the consumer's own walker, cane or lift equipment as instructed in the service plan, gait belts if the agency permits their use, and what to do if the consumer begins to fall. A worker may not use equipment on which he or she has not been demonstrated competent.

Training on meal preparation and feeding (c)(4) covers safe food handling, following diet instructions in the service plan, positioning the consumer, helping a consumer who is eating, and recognizing and reporting choking or swallowing difficulty.
Training on toileting (c)(5) covers privacy, assistance with commodes, bedpans and incontinence products, perineal skin care, infection control and reporting changes in elimination.

Training on assistance with self-administered medications (c)(6) covers the limits on what the worker may do, reminders, opening containers, observing the consumer, documenting any assistance, and the prohibition on selecting, mixing, crushing, injecting or deciding on medications (see SVC-05).

A nurse or qualified supervisor observes the worker performing each task, using a doll, a mannequin, a volunteer or the worker in an actual supervised visit, and rates each step on the Personal Care Skills Checklist as satisfactory or needs improvement.
If any skill is rated 'needs improvement', the evaluator retrains the worker and observes the skill again. The worker is not cleared for that task until it is rated satisfactory.

The evaluator signs and dates the Skills Checklist, and the Administrator signs when the worker is cleared. The Administrator then changes the worker's status to 'Personal care cleared' and tells the scheduler.

Schedulers assign personal care only to workers with 'Personal care cleared' status. If a scheduler or supervisor finds a worker performing personal care without that status, the worker is stopped immediately, the consumer's needs are covered by a cleared worker, and the Administrator documents the event and retrains the worker.

If a consumer needs a personal care task not covered in the worker's checklist, the supervisor trains and checks the worker on that task before the worker performs it unsupervised, and documents the training.

responsibilities.duty: Decides each worker's clearance status, signs the clearance and enforces the no-personal-care rule for uncleared workers.
Observes return demonstrations, completes and signs the Personal Care Skills Checklist and retrains as needed.

Performs only the tasks for which he or she has been cleared, and asks for training before doing any other task.

policies.title: Competency Documentation, Portability and Annual Review
policies.applies_to: All direct care workers; the Administrator, supervisors and the personnel record keeper.
policies.purpose: To make sure each worker's competency is documented in the worker's file, to set rules for accepting competency records from another agency or registry, and to require competency to be reviewed at least once a year and more often after discipline for a quality-of-care infraction.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] documents each worker's satisfactory completion of the competency requirements in the worker's file and keeps a copy of any nurse or other health-professional license or certification the worker holds. This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.55(d): competency documentation is transferable between agencies and registries if the break in employment or roster status is 12 months or less. The agency verifies any transferred record against its own standards. This policy also meets 28 Pa. Code §611.55(e): the agency documents in each worker's file a review of the worker's competency to perform assigned duties at least once per year after initial competency, and more often when discipline or another sanction, such as a verbal warning or suspension, is imposed for a quality-of-care infraction. Methods of review are direct observation, testing, training, consumer feedback, another Department-approved method, or a combination.

definitions.definition: Satisfactory completion of the exam or training required by CMP-02 and, for personal care workers, CMP-03.

definitions.term: Break in employment or roster status
definitions.definition: The time between the end of a worker's employment or roster status at one agency or registry and the start at the next. It is counted in calendar months.
A failure to provide care or services as required by the service plan or agency policy that affected, or could have affected, a consumer's health, safety, dignity or well-being.
A documented review of a worker's competency to perform assigned duties, done at least once in each year after initial competency.

procedures: When a worker completes initial competency, the Administrator or designee places in the worker's file the completed exam or training record, the Personal Care Skills Checklist if applicable, the date of completion and the evaluator's signature.

If the worker holds a nurse or other health-professional license or certification (for example RN, LPN or certified nurse aide), the Administrator copies it, verifies it with the issuing board, files it and records the expiration date on the tracker.

When a worker offers competency documentation from another agency or registry, the Administrator first checks the dates of the worker's last employment or roster status and counts the months of the break.

If the break is 12 months or less, the Administrator reviews the prior documentation against this agency's standards. The prior record must show all topics in CMP-02 and, if the worker will provide personal care, CMP-03. It must also show the evaluator and the date of completion.

If the prior record is accepted, the Administrator files a copy, writes a dated note that the record was verified against agency standards, and arranges agency-specific orientation (PER-02). If the prior record is missing a topic, the worker completes training on the missing topic before assignment.
If the break is more than 12 months, or the prior record cannot be verified, the worker completes the agency's exam or training in full before any consumer contact.
The Administrator keeps a competency tracker listing each worker, the date of initial competency, the date of the last annual review and the next due date. The tracker is reviewed at least monthly.

At least 30 days before the due date, the supervisor schedules the annual review. The review may use direct observation during a supervised visit, a test, refresher training, consumer feedback collected under SVC-04, another Department-approved method, or a combination.

The reviewer records the method(s) used, the date, the topics and duties reviewed, the result and any corrective action, and signs and dates the record. The record is filed in the worker's file within 7 days.
If the review shows a gap, the supervisor provides retraining and re-checks the skill. The worker does not perform the affected task unsupervised until competency is documented.

When a verbal warning, written warning, suspension or other sanction is imposed for a quality-of-care infraction, the supervisor notifies the Administrator the same day. A competency review focused on the infraction is completed within 30 days of the sanction, and before the worker returns to duty if the worker has been suspended.
The Administrator documents the review in the worker's file with a cross-reference to the discipline record, and tracks the next regular annual review date from the most recent review.
A worker whose annual review is overdue is not scheduled for new assignments until the review is done. The Administrator documents any exception in writing, with the reason and the new due date.
Records are available to the Department on request, and the Administrator performs a quarterly audit of the tracker against the worker files.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies transferred competency records, maintains the tracker, makes sure reviews and post-discipline reviews are done and documented, and audits the files.
Performs and documents reviews, collects consumer feedback and retrains where needed.
Files competency documents and licenses and updates the tracker.
Provides prior competency records and any licenses, and takes part in annual reviews.

Copies of any nurse or other health-professional license or certification, with verification

policies.title: Tuberculosis Screening Before Consumer Contact and 12-Month Updates
policies.applies_to: All direct care workers, and any office staff or contractors who have direct consumer contact; the Administrator and the personnel record keeper.
policies.purpose: To protect consumers and workers from tuberculosis by requiring documented screening before consumer contact and regular updates.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.56(a). Before having contact with any consumer, each direct care worker, and any other office staff member or contractor who has direct consumer contact, must give [AGENCY NAME] documentation of screening for, and freedom from, active mycobacterium tuberculosis. Screening follows Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines. The documented screening date may not be more than 1 year before the individual's start date. This policy also meets 28 Pa. Code §611.56(b): the agency requires these individuals to update their TB documentation at least every 12 months, counted from the last evaluation, and keeps the documentation in each individual's file. Anyone whose documentation is missing or lapsed is removed from consumer contact until it is current. TB records are medical information and are kept confidential.

definitions.definition: In-person contact with a consumer in the consumer's home or other service setting, as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5. It includes office staff and contractors who visit or work with consumers.

A CDC-guided evaluation for tuberculosis, usually a symptom review plus a TB skin test or blood test, with a chest X-ray and medical evaluation when a result is positive, performed by a licensed health care provider.
The first day on which the individual will have consumer contact for the agency.
The date of the most recent documented TB screening. The 12-month update period is counted from this date.

procedures: The offer letter and onboarding checklist state that TB screening documentation is required before any consumer contact. This applies to direct care workers and to any office staff or contractor who will have direct consumer contact.
The Administrator tells each new individual that screening must follow current CDC guidelines and must be dated no more than 1 year before the start date. A screening dated earlier must be repeated.

The individual obtains screening from a licensed health care provider, such as a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, clinic or health department, and gives the agency written documentation. The agency may arrange screening on request and pays for it as set out in [AGENCY NAME]'s employee benefit policy.

The documentation must show the individual's name, the type of screening, the date, the result, and the provider's name and signature or stamp. It must state that the individual is free from active TB.

If the screening is positive or the symptom review is positive, the individual is referred to a health care provider for evaluation (such as a chest X-ray). The individual does not have consumer contact until a provider documents in writing that the individual is free from active TB.

Before the first consumer assignment, the Administrator or designee checks the documentation for completeness and for a screening date no more than 1 year before the start date. The reviewer initials and dates the checklist.
No individual is scheduled or sent to a consumer's home, and no consumer contact occurs, until the documentation is in the file. A provisional hire is held to this same rule.

The documentation is filed in the individual's file in the confidential medical section, separate from general personnel information, and is not shared except as permitted by law or required by the Department.
The Administrator records each individual's last evaluation date and the next due date (12 months later) on the TB tracker.
At 60 days and again at 30 days before the due date, the record keeper notifies the individual in writing that updated screening documentation is required. A final notice is sent at 7 days.

The individual submits updated documentation on or before the due date. The record keeper checks it, files it and updates the tracker. The next due date is counted from the date of the new evaluation.

If updated documentation is not on file by the due date, the Administrator removes the individual from consumer contact effective the following day. The scheduler arranges coverage for affected consumers, and the removal is documented.
The individual returns to consumer contact only after current documentation is received and reviewed. The Administrator documents the date of return.

Workers are instructed to report TB symptoms (such as a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, fever, night sweats or weight loss) to the Administrator immediately, and may be asked to obtain a medical evaluation before returning to work. Reports of exposure follow SAF-03.
The Administrator audits the TB tracker against all files monthly and reports exceptions to the governing body quarterly under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no individual has consumer contact without current TB documentation, removes lapsed individuals from contact and audits the tracker.
Reviews and files TB documents, maintains the tracker and sends reminders.
Does not schedule anyone who is not shown as TB-current.

responsibilities.role: Direct care worker, office staff, contractor
responsibilities.duty: Obtains screening and updates on time and reports symptoms or exposure.

Onboarding checklist showing the review date and the reviewer
TB tracker with last evaluation dates and next due dates
Reminder notices and removal-from-contact records
Provider clearance following any positive screening
Monthly audit records

policies.title: Consumer Participation in Service Planning and Reasonable Accommodation
policies.applies_to: All consumers; the Administrator, intake staff, supervisors, schedulers and direct care workers.
policies.purpose: To ensure every consumer takes part in planning his or her services and receives services that reasonably accommodate individual needs and preferences, while protecting the health and safety of direct care workers.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(a)(1). Each consumer of [AGENCY NAME] has the right to be involved in the service planning process and to receive services with reasonable accommodation of individual needs and preferences, except where the direct care worker's health and safety is at risk. The agency respects consumer control as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5. The consumer's participation and preferences are recorded in the service plan. For consumers in Community HealthChoices (CHC) or the OBRA Waiver, the agency's process follows the person-centered service plan developed by the consumer's service coordinator or managed care organization (MCO), in line with the home and community-based services person-centered planning requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c); the agency does not use this policy to lessen any right under that rule. This right is explained to the consumer in the consumer information packet (CP-04 and CP-05).

definitions.definition: The consumer's right to direct the services he or she receives, as defined in 28 Pa. Code §611.5.
The process of deciding what services the consumer will receive, when, how and by whom, written into the service plan (SVC-03).

An adjustment to services, scheduling, communication or the way a task is done that meets the consumer's needs or preferences and does not endanger a worker or conflict with law or the scope of services (SVC-01).
For CHC and OBRA participants, the plan developed with the participant by the service coordinator or MCO, which directs the services the agency delivers.

definitions.term: Health and safety risk to the worker
definitions.definition: A condition that exposes the direct care worker to a real risk of injury, illness, abuse or harassment, as opposed to inconvenience or dislike of a task.

procedures: At intake, the intake coordinator explains to the consumer, and the consumer's representative if there is one, that the consumer has the right to take part in planning and to ask for reasonable accommodation. The explanation is oral and written and uses the consumer's language or format (CR-05).

The assessing supervisor or nurse meets with the consumer (and anyone the consumer chooses to include, such as family or a representative) before services start. The meeting asks about daily routine, goals, cultural and religious needs, communication needs, preferences for how tasks are done, preferred schedule and preferences about workers (such as gender or language).
The consumer, not the agency, decides who participates in planning. The agency does not exclude a consumer who has a representative, and speaks to the consumer first.
The service plan (SVC-03) records the consumer's own goals and preferences in the consumer's words where possible, and records which of the consumer's requests the agency has accommodated.

For CHC and OBRA participants, the supervisor obtains the person-centered service plan from the service coordinator or MCO, confirms that the agency's service plan matches it, and does not change authorized services without the service coordinator or MCO. The supervisor documents how the consumer's preferences are honored. Any conflict is raised with the service coordinator or MCO.

The consumer, or representative, reviews the plan, may request changes and receives a copy. The consumer's signature or documented oral agreement is recorded. A consumer's refusal to sign does not stop services and is documented.

Reasonable requests, such as preferred times, the order of tasks, the manner of performing a task, use of the consumer's own supplies, cultural food practices, and language or communication aids, are accommodated and recorded. The scheduler is told of scheduling preferences the same day.

A request that would require a task outside the agency's scope of services (SVC-01), conflict with the law, or exceed authorized hours is explained to the consumer. The supervisor offers alternatives, refers the consumer to the proper provider or service coordinator, and documents the discussion.

A request may be declined only if it places the direct care worker's health and safety at risk. Examples are a hostile or unsafe environment, harassment, unsafe equipment or a request to perform a task that the worker has not been trained or cleared to do. The supervisor decides with the Administrator, tells the consumer why, offers alternatives such as correcting the hazard or changing the worker, and documents the reasons.

Before declining on safety grounds, the supervisor checks whether the risk can be removed by a reasonable measure (training, equipment, a second worker). If it cannot, any decision to reduce or stop services follows CP-02.

Direct care workers are trained to follow the service plan and the consumer's expressed preferences, to report new preferences or problems to the supervisor, and not to promise changes that have not been approved.

At each supervisory visit and at least every [SUPERVISORY VISIT INTERVAL], the supervisor asks the consumer whether services reflect his or her preferences and whether anything needs to change, and updates the plan (SVC-03, SVC-04).
A consumer who believes that his or her participation or preferences are not being respected may file a grievance under CR-02. No consumer is retaliated against for making a request or complaint.
The Administrator reviews a sample of service plans each quarter for evidence of consumer participation and documented accommodations, and reports the results under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures this right is followed, decides with the supervisor when an accommodation cannot be made for worker safety reasons, and reviews plans quarterly.
Explains the right to participate and to reasonable accommodation at intake.
Conducts the planning meeting, documents participation, preferences and accommodations, and coordinates with the service coordinator or MCO.
Applies scheduling and worker preferences where possible.
Follows the plan, respects the consumer's choices and reports changes or concerns.

documentation: Signed or documented acknowledgment that the right was explained to the consumer
Service plan showing consumer participation, preferences and accommodations
Person-centered service plan from the service coordinator or MCO for CHC and OBRA participants
Record of requests that were declined, with the reason and the alternatives offered
Notes of supervisory visits and plan reviews
Quarterly service plan audit results

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services: 10-Day Written Notice
policies.applies_to: All consumers; the Administrator, supervisors, intake and billing staff.
policies.purpose: To protect consumers from abrupt loss of services by requiring advance written notice of termination, to limit the exceptions to the notice period, and to support safe transitions.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(a)(2). [AGENCY NAME] gives each consumer at least 10 calendar days' advance written notice of its intent to terminate services. Shorter notice is allowed only in two situations: (1) the consumer, despite notice, has failed to pay and is more than 14 days in arrears; or (2) the direct care worker's health and welfare is at risk. For Medicaid participants in Community HealthChoices (CHC) or the OBRA Waiver, the agency also notifies the service coordinator or managed care organization (MCO) and helps with the transition to another provider. The reason for termination, the notice date and the transition steps are documented in the client record. Separately, if the agency decides to stop providing a health care service it offers, it notifies the Department in writing at least 60 days beforehand as required by 28 Pa. Code §51.3(a) and (c), and tells affected consumers.

definitions.definition: A decision by the agency to end, or to stop providing, all services to a consumer. It includes discharge and transfer to another provider.
Every day, including weekends and holidays. The notice period begins the day after the notice is delivered or mailed.
Unpaid charges owed to the agency by a private-pay consumer. It does not apply to a Medicaid participant whose services are paid by a managed care organization or the Commonwealth.
The person who coordinates a participant's services under CHC (through the MCO) or the OBRA Waiver.

definitions.term: Worker health and welfare at risk
definitions.definition: A situation in which the worker is, or is reasonably expected to be, in danger of harm, including violence, threats, abuse, harassment, or a serious and uncorrected health or safety hazard in the home.

procedures: Before any termination decision, the supervisor documents the problem, the steps already taken to solve it (for example a care conference, a change of worker, correction of a hazard) and the consumer's response. The agency tries to resolve the problem where it can safely be done.

The Administrator alone makes the decision to terminate and records the reason: non-payment, safety risk to the worker, change in needs beyond the agency's scope (SVC-01), consumer request, loss of payer authorization or any other reason, in the client record.
A termination is never based on a complaint, a grievance, a request for accommodation or a report to the Department or other agency made by the consumer or the consumer's family.

Standard notice: the Administrator gives the consumer, and the representative if any, written notice at least 10 calendar days before the termination date. The notice states the reason, the last date of service, the consumer's right to submit a grievance (CR-02), the agency contact, and information about finding other providers.

The notice is delivered in person with a signed receipt, or mailed with proof of mailing, and sent by email or text if the consumer has agreed to this in writing. The notice is written in the consumer's language or format (CR-05). The agency counts the 10 days from the day after delivery or mailing, and adds time if mailing is used.

Non-payment exception: Notice of non-payment is given in writing first. The agency may end services on shorter notice only if the consumer, despite that notice, has failed to pay and the unpaid balance is more than 14 days in arrears. The billing office documents the dates, amounts and notices, and the Administrator approves the shorter notice in writing.

Worker safety exception: If a worker's health and welfare is at risk, the Administrator may shorten the notice or end services immediately. The worker is removed from the home first. The Administrator documents the facts, who reported them, and why the safety risk could not be resolved. Written notice, stating the reason, is given the same day or the next business day. If the consumer is in immediate danger without care, the supervisor arranges emergency help (SVC-08) and informs the service coordinator or MCO.

For CHC or OBRA participants, the Administrator notifies the service coordinator or MCO in writing on the same day as the consumer and works with them to find another provider. Services are not ended until a safe transition is in place, except under the worker safety exception. The agency does not bill the participant for covered services.

For all consumers, the supervisor helps with the transition by offering a list of other agencies, speaking with the consumer's family, representative or physician if the consumer agrees, and sending care information and the service plan to the new provider on written request or consent (CR-03).
The agency continues to provide services according to the plan throughout the notice period, unless the consumer declines or the worker safety exception applies.
If the consumer asks to end services, the supervisor confirms the request in writing, documents the date and offers help with the transition.

If the agency loses its ability to provide a service entirely (for example, closing a service line), the Administrator notifies the Department in writing at least 60 days before ceasing the service, as required by 28 Pa. Code §51.3(a) and (c), and notifies affected consumers and service coordinators or MCOs in writing with at least the 10-day notice. The agency helps each consumer transition to another provider.

The Administrator completes a termination record within 3 business days of the end of service. The record includes the reason, copies of notices and proof of delivery, the notice date, the date of the last service, contacts with the service coordinator or MCO, and the transition steps taken.
Records are retained according to REC-01. The Administrator reviews every termination quarterly and reports the findings to the governing body under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Makes termination decisions, approves any shortened notice, issues the notices and the notice to the Department where required, and oversees transitions.
Documents problems and resolution efforts, assists with transition and arranges for emergency care where needed.
Documents arrears and notices for private-pay accounts.
Contacts the service coordinator or MCO and other providers to arrange a transition.

documentation: Written termination notice with the reason and the dates
Proof of delivery or mailing
Documentation of the reason, including arrears records or safety incident report if a shortened notice is used
Notice to the service coordinator or MCO and transition records for Medicaid participants
Transition referrals and consent for record release
Termination record with the Administrator's signature
Written notice to the Department under 28 Pa. Code §51.3 where the agency ceases a service

policies.title: Prohibition on Power of Attorney, Guardianship and Check Endorsement
policies.applies_to: Owners, governing body, Administrator, office staff, supervisors, direct care workers, contractors and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect consumers from financial and legal control by the agency or the people who work for it, and to meet the consumer protection prohibitions in 28 Pa. Code §611.57(b).
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(b) (Prohibitions). No one may assume power of attorney or guardianship over a consumer by reason of affiliation with [AGENCY NAME]. This applies to owners, governing body members, the Administrator, office staff, supervisors and direct care workers. [AGENCY NAME] will not require a consumer to endorse checks over to the agency. As agency policy, no staff member may serve as a consumer's agent, representative payee or financial power of attorney while employed by or affiliated with the agency. Any request or offer of such an arrangement, from either side, must be reported to the Administrator. Consumers pay the agency by their own check or electronic payment made out to the agency. They are never asked to sign over a government benefit, pension, insurance or other check they receive.

definitions.definition: A legal document that authorizes a person to act as another's agent in financial, legal or health care matters.
A court-ordered appointment of a person to make decisions for an individual found incapacitated.
A person or organization appointed by a benefit-paying agency to receive and manage a beneficiary's benefit payments.
Signing the back of a check to transfer it to another party. For this policy, it means having a consumer sign over a check payable to the consumer so the agency receives the funds.
Any owner, governing body member, officer, employee, supervisor, direct care worker, contractor or volunteer of the agency.

procedures: At hire and at each annual review, the Administrator gives every affiliated person a copy of this policy. The person signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record (see PER-03).

During orientation, the Administrator or designee trains direct care workers to decline any request to act as POA, guardian, representative payee or financial agent. They are told to offer a neutral statement: 'Agency policy and Pennsylvania regulation do not allow me to do that. Please speak with your family, an attorney or your Area Agency on Aging.'

The Intake Coordinator checks each Service Agreement and every form used at intake before it is issued. No form may contain a POA, guardianship, representative payee or check-endorsement clause that names the agency or any affiliated person.
The Intake Coordinator tells each consumer, at intake and in the information packet (see CP-04), that the agency does not seek and will not accept authority over the consumer's affairs.

Billing staff collect private-pay fees only by a check or electronic payment drawn on the consumer's or payer's own account and made payable to [AGENCY NAME]. They never ask a consumer to endorse a Social Security, pension, insurance or other third-party check to the agency.
Medicaid payments (Community HealthChoices and OBRA Waiver) go to the agency from the managed care organization or payer. They are never routed through a consumer's check (see SVC-09).

If a consumer or family member asks an affiliated person to serve as POA, guardian, payee or agent, the person declines politely. The person reports the request to the Administrator the same day, or by the next business day if the Administrator is unavailable.

If an affiliated person is asked to hold or sign a consumer's check, or is offered such authority, the person reports it to the Administrator within the same timeframe. The Administrator documents it on an incident or concern report.

The Administrator reviews each report within 2 business days. Possible actions include contacting the consumer or representative, explaining the policy, and referring the family to the Area Agency on Aging or an attorney.

If the consumer already has a POA or guardian who is not affiliated with the agency, the agency works with that person and keeps a copy of the document in the record. The agency does not name any affiliated person as agent or successor agent.

If a staff member is a relative of a consumer who already holds a POA or guardianship from before employment, the Administrator reviews it with legal counsel before assignment. The Administrator documents the review and takes steps so the arrangement is not used to avoid this policy.

Any staff member who assumes or attempts to assume such authority, or who asks a consumer to endorse a check, is removed from the consumer's case immediately. The matter is investigated, and discipline up to termination applies. Suspected exploitation follows SAF-01 and CR-04.

The Administrator reviews the consumer's file at each supervisory visit or plan update. The review confirms that no document names an affiliated person as the consumer's agent, guardian, payee or check endorser.
The Administrator records all reports and outcomes in the CP-06 compliance file.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt this policy and make sure no ownership or management practice conflicts with it.
Train staff, review reports within 2 business days, apply discipline, and keep records.
Keep forms free of prohibited clauses and explain the policy to consumers.
Accept payments only in the allowed ways and never request check endorsement.

responsibilities.role: Direct Care Workers and all staff
responsibilities.duty: Decline requests, never hold or sign a consumer's checks, and report requests or offers to the Administrator.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy
Reports of requests or offers of POA, guardianship, payee or check endorsement, with the Administrator's findings and actions
Copies of any consumer-held POA or guardianship documents held by non-affiliated persons
Quarterly file audit results (see CP-06)
Disciplinary records, if any

policies.title: Consumer Information Packet: Delivery, Services, Hours and Fees
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Intake Coordinator, Scheduler, supervisors and billing staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every consumer receives, before services begin, an easy-to-read information packet that states what services will be provided and by whom, when services will be provided, and what they will cost.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(c) (Information packet before services begin) and items (c)(1), (c)(2) and (c)(3). Before any services begin, [AGENCY NAME] gives the consumer, the consumer's legal representative or a responsible family member an easy-to-read information packet and obtains a signed acknowledgment. The packet contains item (c)(1), a listing of the available home care services that the direct care worker will provide and the identity of the worker who will provide them. It contains item (c)(2), the hours when services will be provided. It contains item (c)(3), fees and total costs for the services on an hourly or weekly basis. The remaining packet items, (c)(4) through (c)(7), are covered in policy CP-05 and are delivered in the same packet. Services do not start until the packet has been delivered. The relevant pages are reissued whenever the worker, hours or fees change.

definitions.definition: The written, easy-to-read set of consumer information required by 28 Pa. Code §611.57(c), delivered before services begin.
A relative or other person the consumer identifies as involved in the consumer's care and authorized by the consumer to receive information.
A person with legal authority to act for the consumer, such as a guardian or an agent under a power of attorney who is not affiliated with the agency (see CP-03).

The full amount the consumer will be responsible for, on an hourly or weekly basis. It includes any minimum-hour requirements and any additional charges. It may be $0 when a payer covers all authorized hours.

procedures: The Intake Coordinator prepares the packet for each new consumer using the agency's current packet template, which has been approved by the Administrator. The packet is written in plain language at about a 6th–8th grade reading level, in at least 12-point type, with headings and short sentences.
The Intake Coordinator offers the packet in the consumer's preferred language or format (large print, interpreter or read aloud) and records the choice (see CR-05).

Item (c)(1): The Intake Coordinator lists the home care services the consumer will receive, taken from the service plan and consistent with the scope of services in SVC-01. The packet also gives the name of the direct care worker assigned. If a worker is not yet assigned, the Scheduler assigns one before the packet is delivered, because services may not begin without the worker being named.
Item (c)(2): The Scheduler enters the days and hours of service, including start and end times and any planned changes, from the authorization or service agreement.

Item (c)(3): The Billing Coordinator enters the fees and total costs. For private pay, this is the hourly rate [HOURLY RATE] and the weekly cost for the scheduled hours, plus any minimum-hour requirement or other charge disclosed in the Service Agreement (see CR-06). For Community HealthChoices or OBRA Waiver consumers, the packet shows the payer, the authorized hours, and the consumer's cost, if any, confirmed against the payer authorization (see SVC-09).
The Administrator reviews the completed packet for accuracy, including that the fees match the Service Agreement and that the worker and hours match the schedule, before it is delivered.

The packet is delivered to the consumer, legal representative or responsible family member before the first service visit. It is delivered in person at the home or office or by mail or secure electronic means with confirmation of receipt.
The staff member delivering the packet reviews the contents with the recipient, answers questions, and tells the recipient they may keep the packet.

The recipient signs and dates the acknowledgment of receipt. If the recipient cannot or will not sign, the staff member writes the reason on the acknowledgment, signs it, and has a second staff member initial it.

The Scheduler does not release the first visit until the Administrator or Intake Coordinator confirms in the file that the signed acknowledgment is on hand or that the exception has been documented and approved by the Administrator.

When the assigned worker changes (including temporary substitutes expected to work more than a single visit), the Scheduler tells the consumer before the new worker starts. The Intake Coordinator reissues the (c)(1) page with the new worker's name, and the consumer signs a new acknowledgment.
When hours change by agreement, authorization or payer action, the Scheduler or Intake Coordinator reissues the (c)(2) page within 2 business days and no later than the first changed visit.
When fees or total costs change, the Billing Coordinator reissues the (c)(3) page and Service Agreement addendum before the new fees take effect. The consumer signs an acknowledgment.
The original signed acknowledgment and a copy of the packet and any reissued pages are filed in the consumer's compliance file (see CP-06) and client record (see REC-01) within 2 business days.

responsibilities.duty: Approve the packet template, review each completed packet for accuracy, and authorize any exception for a missing signature.
Prepare and deliver the packet, obtain the signed acknowledgment, and reissue pages.
Assign the worker, enter hours, and withhold the first visit until delivery is confirmed.
Calculate and enter fees and total costs and notify the Intake Coordinator of fee changes.
Refer packet questions to the office and tell the office promptly if the consumer reports not having received the packet.

documentation: Signed packet acknowledgment (date, recipient name and relationship, staff member)
Copy of the packet as delivered, with the (c)(1), (c)(2) and (c)(3) pages and dates
Reissued pages and new acknowledgments for each change of worker, hours or fees
Record of language or format accommodation
Administrator exception approvals, if any

policies.title: Consumer Information Packet: Department Contacts, Complaint Line, Hiring Standards and Worker Status Disclosure
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Intake Coordinator, supervisors and billing staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure the information packet gives each consumer the Department of Health contacts, the complaint Hot Line and Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman number, the agency's hiring and competency requirements, and the required employee or independent-contractor disclosure.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(c)(4), (c)(5), (c)(6) and (c)(7). Each information packet delivered under CP-04 before services begin includes the following. Item (c)(4) is who to contact at the Pennsylvania Department of Health for information about licensure requirements and for compliance information about [AGENCY NAME]. Item (c)(5) is the Department's complaint Hot Line and the telephone number of the local Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman Program. Item (c)(6) is the hiring and competency requirements that apply to the direct care workers employed by the agency. Item (c)(7) is a disclosure, in the format published by the Department in the Pennsylvania Bulletin, on the worker's employee versus independent-contractor status and the resulting tax, insurance and other obligations of the consumer and the agency. [AGENCY NAME] employs its direct care workers as W-2 employees and does not use independent contractors to provide care, and the packet says so. The packet is delivered and acknowledged as described in CP-04.

definitions.definition: The Department of Health's toll-free line for complaints about licensed home care agencies and registries.
The local long-term care ombudsman program of the Area Agency on Aging serving the consumer's county.

A worker whose wages the agency pays through payroll, with withholding of taxes, and for whom the agency carries employer obligations such as unemployment compensation contributions and workers' compensation coverage.
A worker in business for themselves, who is not an employee of the agency. [AGENCY NAME] does not use independent contractors to deliver direct care.

procedures: Before the first packet is issued, and after any change to the regulation, the Administrator confirms the adopted text of §611.57(c)(4)–(c)(7) and the Department's current Pennsylvania Bulletin format for the (c)(7) disclosure with the Department's Division of Home Health. The Administrator files a dated note of the confirmation in the compliance file.

Item (c)(4): The Administrator maintains the Department contact page. It names the Department of Health, Bureau of Health Care Facilities and Home Care Services, Division of Home Health, as the contact for licensure requirements and for compliance information about [AGENCY NAME]. It lists the phone number [DOH DIVISION PHONE, confirmed on the date noted in the compliance file] and email ra-dhhlicenquestions@pa.gov, and tells the consumer they may ask the Department for [AGENCY NAME]'s license and inspection information.

Item (c)(5): The Administrator maintains the complaint page. The Department's Hot Line number is printed exactly as it appears in the current §611.57(c)(5) text. The Department's published checklist lists 1-800-254-5164, and Department consumer materials list 1-866-826-3644. Before each print run, the Administrator calls or checks the Department's website to verify which number is current and records the date and result. No packet is printed until this is done.

Item (c)(5): The Intake Coordinator identifies the consumer's county and enters the telephone number of the local Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman Program, [LOCAL AAA OMBUDSMAN PHONE], in the packet for that consumer. The Administrator verifies the AAA numbers for all counties served at least every 6 months and whenever a caller reports a wrong number.

Items (c)(4) and (c)(5): The packet also gives the agency's own complaint contact, [PHONE], and says that a consumer may contact the Department or the Ombudsman at any time, with or without first contacting the agency, and will not be retaliated against (see CR-02).

Item (c)(6): The Administrator maintains a one-page, plain-language summary of the hiring and competency requirements that apply to the agency's direct care workers. It is drawn from the agency's hiring and competency policies (HIR-01, HIR-02, CBC-01 to CBC-04, CAC-01, PRV-01, PRV-02, CMP-01 to CMP-04, HS-01) and covers the interview and references, required criminal history reports, ChildLine verification where applicable, tuberculosis screening, and competency testing before assignment.
Item (c)(6): The Administrator updates the summary within 30 days of any change to those policies or to the applicable regulation and re-dates the page.

Item (c)(7): The Intake Coordinator inserts the Department's published disclosure on employee versus independent-contractor status in the Department's format. The packet states that the assigned worker is an employee of [AGENCY NAME] and that the agency withholds payroll taxes, pays employer taxes and unemployment compensation contributions, and carries workers' compensation coverage as required by law. It also states that the consumer is not the worker's employer for those purposes.

Item (c)(7): If the agency ever proposes to use any worker other than a W-2 employee, the Administrator must first obtain written approval from the Governing Body and revise this policy. The consumer disclosure must then be changed before that worker is assigned.

The Intake Coordinator assembles items (c)(4) through (c)(7) with items (c)(1) through (c)(3) from CP-04 into a single packet and delivers it before services begin. The consumer, legal representative or responsible family member signs the acknowledgment, which lists each item.

The Administrator reviews every packet template and the contact pages at least annually and whenever the Department changes a number, address or disclosure format. Old versions are marked superseded and retained.
Copies of the signed acknowledgment and packet are filed in the compliance file (see CP-06) and client record within 2 business days of delivery.

responsibilities.duty: Confirm regulatory text and the Department's disclosure format, verify the Hot Line and Department contact details before each print run, and maintain the (c)(6) summary.
Insert the correct county AAA Ombudsman number, assemble and deliver the complete packet, and obtain the signed acknowledgment.
Confirm that all direct care workers are W-2 employees and that payroll tax and insurance statements in the disclosure are accurate.
Approve any change to worker classification before it takes effect.

documentation: Signed packet acknowledgment listing items (c)(1)–(c)(7)
Dated record of Hot Line, Department contact and AAA Ombudsman number verification
Dated confirmation of the adopted regulation text and Department disclosure format
Current and superseded versions of the (c)(6) summary and the (c)(7) disclosure
Copy of packet as delivered to each consumer

policies.title: Documentation of Compliance with Consumer Protections
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Intake Coordinator, records staff and supervisors of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep organized proof that [AGENCY NAME] complies with each consumer protection in 28 Pa. Code §611.57, available for Department of Health inspection at any time.
policies.policy: This policy meets 28 Pa. Code §611.57(d) (Documentation). [AGENCY NAME] keeps documentation on file at the agency that shows compliance with §611.57, and keeps it available for Department inspection. The compliance file includes signed information packet acknowledgments, termination notices with proof of delivery, and the worker status disclosures. The Administrator audits a sample of new client files every quarter and corrects any gaps.

definitions.definition: The record, kept for each consumer and in summary by the agency, that shows how the agency met each requirement of §611.57.
